title: Dedicated autoscaler: token-bucket smoothing, per-tenant burst ceilings, and improved utilization reporting
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: fleet autoscaler token-bucket burst behavior can cause short-lived large provisioning spikes during traffic variance which increases cost and destabilizes node placement. This PR implements a token-bucket smoothing layer plus per-tenant burst ceilings and expands utilization reporting to make burst behavior observable. Changes: 1) tokenbucket: introduce an exponentially-weighted moving-average (EWMA) refill smoothing to prevent abrupt token refills; 2) tenant-level burst ceilings: new config field `burst_ceiling_tokens` and enforcement in the allocator to cap short-term burst allocations per tenant; 3) leak-rate telemetry: emit burst_leak_rate and burst_utilization metrics to help SREs tune ceilings; 4) rollout flags: feature-flag gated (default enabled for dedicated fleets v2) with canary rollout tooling in the autoscaler controller; 5) tests and benchmarks: unit tests for tokenbucket transitions, integration e2e sims with synthetic traffic, and loadbench perf scripts. Backwards compatibility: all fields are additive and default to previous behavior when unset so no breaking changes for existing clusters. Rollout plan: canary on 3 low-volume fleets for 48 hours, monitor burst_utilization and allocator stability, then gradual regional rollouts. Summary of results: local perf lab shows 7% median tail latency improvement under synthetic spiky load, 12% reduction in peak GPU allocation across synthetic tenants with mixed burstiness, and no throughput regressions. CI: build + unit + integration + perf-bench passed after minor test fix. See linked Linear tasks for follow-ups (tuning defaults, dashboard migrations).
commits: feat(autoscaler): add tokenbucket EWMA smoothing and parameters
feat(allocator): enforce per-tenant burst_ceiling_tokens during allocation
feat(metrics): emit burst_leak_rate and burst_utilization metrics
chore(config): add burst_ceiling_tokens to dedicated fleet spec proto and defaults
test(autoscaler): add unit tests for smoothing behavior and ceiling enforcement
perf(loadbench): add synthetic mixed-tenant workload for burst scenarios
docs: document new configs and rollout playbook
review_comments: Tomás Rivera: Can we ensure the EWMA window is configurable per-fleet? In some high-churn fleets the default 30s window may be too long.
Aisha Patel: Yes, added `smoothing_window_seconds` to the fleet spec with a sensible default of 30s and per-fleet override in the controller.
Michael Chen: The enforcement path in allocator looks correct, but we should avoid starving short lived internal control-plane bursts (health-checks). Add an allowlist for system tenants.
Aisha Patel: Added system tenant allowlist bypass and unit tests to validate no starvation.
Priya Nair: Metrics look useful, would be good to expose a derived SLO signal for `burst_utilization > ceiling` so ops can auto-alert.
Aisha Patel: Added a recommendation in the docs and dashboard JSON for an alert rule `burst_utilization > 0.9 for 5m` and we plan to wire it into the console in a follow-up ENG-4300.
release_notes: Autoscaler: token-bucket EWMA smoothing to reduce sudden provisioning spikes
Autoscaler: per-tenant burst ceilings to cap short-term allocations
Observability: new metrics burst_leak_rate and burst_utilization
Config: new fleet spec fields burst_ceiling_tokens and smoothing_window_seconds
